studies.label: Forest cover classification
studies.question: One boosted model, or a forest ensemble?
studies.description: Predict forest-cover categories from synthetic tabular measurements. Compare the models, tree sizes, training samples, and stopping rules chosen by the six policies.
studies.takeaway: UCB’s five-forest vote reaches a higher test percentile than BoN’s single boosted model in this run. The other programs vary tree size, training-data use, and boosting rounds.

solutions.title: Boost trees with early stopping
solutions.description: Trains LightGBM for up to 200 boosting rounds, with a depth limit of eight. Validation loss determines the prediction checkpoint.

solutions.title: Train 100 boosting rounds
solutions.description: Fits one LightGBM classifier with 100 boosting rounds, up to 31 leaves per tree, and a depth limit of ten.

solutions.title: Let five random forests vote
solutions.description: Fits five random forests with 300 trees each and different random seeds, then chooses the majority class prediction for each row.

solutions.title: Allow larger boosted trees
solutions.description: Fits 150 LightGBM boosting rounds on 90% of the training rows, allowing up to 50 leaves per tree and a depth limit of 25.
steps: Allow up to 50 leaves per tree

solutions.title: Train on a smaller sample
solutions.description: Samples 500,000 rows, holds out 20%, and trains 100 LightGBM boosting rounds with shallow trees and balanced class weights.
solutions.note: After the holdout split, the model fits 400,000 rows.

solutions.title: Train 200 rounds with shallow trees
solutions.description: Fits 200 LightGBM boosting rounds on 80% of the training rows, with a depth limit of six and learning rate of 0.05.

studies.label: Author identification
studies.question: Which writing patterns reveal the author?
studies.description: Given a passage, predict its author. The six programs differ in the patterns they extract, the classifier they fit, and how they combine predictions.
studies.takeaway: The differences go beyond model size: explicit writing-style features, Naive Bayes, model blending, and longer or word-boundary character patterns.

solutions.title: Add writing-style features
solutions.description: Adds length, punctuation, capitalization, and vocabulary statistics to word and character patterns, then fits logistic regression.

solutions.title: Blend two text classifiers
solutions.description: Trains logistic regression and Naive Bayes on word and character patterns. Chooses a geometric blend using validation loss.

solutions.title: Tune a Naive Bayes classifier
solutions.description: Uses word and character TF-IDF features, compares five smoothing strengths, and selects a Naive Bayes model by validation loss.
steps: Fit the selected Naive Bayes model

solutions.title: Average regularization strengths
solutions.description: Combines word and character patterns, then averages three logistic regressions with different regularization settings: C = 0.5, 1, and 5.

solutions.title: Expand the pattern vocabulary
solutions.description: Uses character patterns up to seven characters long and up to 200,000 features per word/character family, with class-balanced logistic regression.

solutions.title: Keep patterns within word boundaries
solutions.description: Combines character patterns within word boundaries with word trigrams. Fits balanced logistic regression with C = 10 and averages three fits.
solutions.note: The repeated fits change the seed but use the same deterministic solver; no ensemble-diversity gain is implied.

selection: Two tasks selected for different solution strategies and higher UCB than BoN percentiles in the displayed runs. Each includes Base AIDE and all five TTS policies with run seed 34. TTS runs are ungated; Base AIDE uses the historical reference. Percentiles belong to the individual saved programs, not seed averages. These selected examples do not establish an overall policy ranking.
